description: A corrected BERT4Rec baseline for four Amazon categories: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. Each category has one independently trained bidirectional Transformer using masked-item training and appended-mask next-item inference. Selection uses macro-average validation HR@10.
motivation: Establish a consistent BERT4Rec starting point for controlled recommendation experiments while preventing target leakage, padding errors, evaluator changes, and checkpoint–predictor mismatches.
implementation_notes: Use preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42, with at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Retain supplied splits, category routing, single-GPU execution, and DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Reserve a mask token, hide prediction targets during training, and read the final nonpadding position in left-padded sequences. Keep the trained architecture and embedded predictor consistent. Preserve ModelView compatibility and the required DiagnosisProbe and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt interfaces. Load exactly one trained model per category; do not fuse independent models or separately fitted scores. No implementation, measured results, or external paper was supplied.
pseudocode:
set preprocessing_seed = 0 and training_seed = 42
for category in the four supplied categories:
    load the supplied training and validation splits
    initialize one BERT4Rec model with a reserved mask token
    for epoch in range(max_epochs <= 200):
        for batch in range(200):
            sample training histories
            construct left-padded masked-item inputs and hidden targets
            optimize masked-target prediction loss
        validate using the fixed protocol and retain one selected checkpoint
    save architecture configuration and selected checkpoint
write a predictor matching the trained architecture
on prediction:
    route to the category model
    append a mask token to the observed history
    truncate and left-pad to the configured length
    score candidate items from the final mask representation
report macro-average validation HR@10 through the host evaluator

originality.positive: Provides a carefully constrained, family-correct experimental baseline.
originality.negative: On a 1–10 scale, originality is low: no new architecture, objective, or research mechanism is described.

future_potential.positive: Supports controlled exploration of masking, regularization, architecture, and optimization within a single BERT4Rec model.
future_potential.negative: On a 1–10 scale, potential is moderate; improvements remain unverified and must fit the shared training budget.

code_difficulty.positive: The model and masked-item objective are established and have a clear implementation structure.
code_difficulty.negative: On a 1–10 difficulty scale, integration is moderately demanding because padding, leakage prevention, diagnostic compatibility, and predictor serialization must agree.
